title: Kidney Immunofluorescence Patterns and Anti-PLA2R Kinetics
summary: Learn the signature immunofluorescence patterns of lupus nephritis, membranous nephropathy, IgA nephropathy and C3 glomerulopathy, why C4d does not exclude C3 glomerulopathy, why mesangial IgA needs a search for secondary causes, and how anti-PLA2R antibody levels behave through remission and relapse.

reviewer.note: Teaches Ch. 55 Hits 3 (anti-PLA2R), 4 (lupus nephritis full house) and 13 (C3 glomerulopathy) and Traps 3 (single anti-PLA2R level) and 5 (mesangial IgA). Checked against Akiyama 2019, Tesar 2021, the 2013 C3 glomerulopathy consensus report (Pickering 2013), Singh 2019, Ye 2023, Knoppova 2021, Tota 2023 and Wang 2020. Discrepancies: the reviewer calls C4d (negative/trace in 90% of C3G) a clean discriminator, but Singh 2019 found C4d negative/trace in only 22% of DDD and 64% of C3GN and concluded C4d should not exclude C3G (register rv-c4d-c3g-discriminator); the reviewer presents PLA2R epitope spreading as a prognostic tool, but Tesar 2021 notes epitope-specific assays are not available in clinical practice (register rv-pla2r-epitope-assay); the reviewer frames a single anti-PLA2R level as non-prognostic, but Tesar 2021 reports that a high baseline titre predicts poorer response, so the lesson teaches baseline plus trend (register rv-pla2r-baseline-titre). Not taught as fact: “intense C1q” as the lupus tell, that no other GN shows a full house, the 180 kDa receptor size, IgAN progression figures, the NIH activity/chronicity indices and lupus serology.

objectives: Match full-house, granular IgG/C3, mesangial IgA and dominant-C3 immunofluorescence patterns to their diseases.
Describe how anti-PLA2R antibody levels change through remission and relapse and why serial measurement is used.
Explain why C4d staining does not exclude C3 glomerulopathy and why mesangial IgA deposits need a search for secondary causes.

scenes.title: Three biopsies and a falling titre
scenes.altText: Invented scenario: three kidney biopsy immunofluorescence reports and one serum result. Biopsy A: IgG, IgA, IgM, C3 and C1q all at least 1+. Biopsy B: C3 3+, IgM 1+, no IgG or C1q; C4d 1+. Biopsy C: mesangial IgA-dominant deposits with C3, in a patient with liver cirrhosis. Serum: a patient with primary membranous nephropathy whose anti-PLA2R antibody has fallen to undetectable while proteinuria persists. Question token: “Which pattern, which disease, which caution?”

cues.text: Three kidney biopsies arrive. Biopsy A stains for everything: IgG, IgA, IgM, C3 and C1q. Biopsy B is mostly C3, with a little IgM and some C4d.
Biopsy C shows mesangial IgA, in a patient with cirrhosis. And a membranous nephropathy patient has lost anti-PLA2R antibody but still leaks protein.
Which pattern points to which disease, and where is the trap in each?

props.label: Which pattern, which disease, which caution?

scenes.title: Four signature stains
scenes.altText: Schematic: four cards. Full house (classic lupus nephritis): IgG, IgA, IgM, C3 and C1q, plus kappa and lambda. Membranous nephropathy: granular IgG (mostly IgG4) and C3 along the glomerular basement membrane; in primary disease the target is often the podocyte phospholipase A2 receptor (PLA2R), less often THSD7A. IgA nephropathy: IgA dominant or co-dominant in the mesangium; C3 is found in most cases (alternative pathway involvement) while C1q is usually absent. C3 glomerulopathy: dominant C3 with little or no immunoglobulin, reflecting abnormal control of complement.

cues.text: Each disease leaves a signature on immunofluorescence. Lupus nephritis classically shows the full house: IgG, IgA, IgM, C3 and C1q together.
Membranous nephropathy shows granular IgG, mostly IgG4, with C3 along the basement membrane. In primary disease the antibody usually targets the podocyte receptor PLA2R.
IgA nephropathy deposits IgA in the mesangium. C3 is usually present, pointing to the alternative pathway, while C1q is usually absent.
C3 glomerulopathy is the opposite of the full house: C3 dominates, with little or no immunoglobulin, because complement control itself has failed.

scenes.title: Anti-PLA2R: follow the film, not the photo
scenes.altText: Timeline schematic (after Akiyama 2019 and Tesar 2021): anti-PLA2R antibodies are found at presentation in about 70–80% of primary membranous nephropathy and are highly specific for it. Early on, antibody may bind the kidney before it is detectable in serum (“kidney as a sink”). With treatment, antibody falls and disappears months before proteinuria resolves (immunologic remission precedes clinical remission). Reappearance or a rise in a previously falling titre signals impending relapse, sometimes before proteinuria rises. Serial measurement (monthly, or at least every two months, during and at the end of treatment) is suggested; ELISA is the recommended method. Epitope spreading from the outer CysR domain to inner CTLD domains is linked with older age and poorer response, but epitope-specific assays are not available in routine practice.

cues.text: Anti-PLA2R antibody is found at presentation in about seventy to eighty percent of primary membranous nephropathy, and it is highly specific for it. Early on, the kidney can soak up the antibody, so serum may still be negative.
With treatment, the antibody falls and disappears months before the proteinuria clears. This is immunologic remission, and it comes before clinical remission.
If the antibody comes back, or a falling titre rises again, relapse is coming, sometimes before the proteinuria rises. That is why serial ELISA measurements are suggested.
Antibodies that spread from the outer CysR domain to inner domains go with poorer response, but epitope assays are not routine, so in practice you follow the titre.

props.title: At diagnosis
lines: Early: kidney acts as a sink

scenes.title: Reading C3, C4d and IgA
scenes.altText: Card 1, dominant C3 (2013 consensus): C3c intensity at least two steps greater than any other immune reactant on a 0, trace, 1+, 2+, 3+ scale is called “glomerulonephritis with dominant C3”; this identifies most C3 glomerulopathy, but post-infectious glomerulonephritis can look the same, so the clinical course and other features matter. Card 2, C4d: absent C4d supports an alternative-pathway process, but in one cohort C4d was negative or trace in only 22% of dense deposit disease and 64% of C3 glomerulonephritis, so C4d staining does not exclude C3 glomerulopathy. Card 3, secondary IgA: liver disease (especially cirrhosis) is the most common trigger of secondary IgA nephropathy; gastrointestinal disease including IBD, infections and other conditions also cause it, and secondary cases share galactose-deficient IgA1 features. Hook answers: A full house = lupus nephritis pattern; B C3 3+ vs IgM 1+ = dominant C3, C4d does not rule out C3 glomerulopathy; C cirrhosis = look for secondary IgA nephropathy; serum = immunologic remission before clinical remission.

cues.text: Dominant C3 means C3 at least two steps brighter than anything else, on a scale of zero, trace, one plus to three plus. This flags most C3 glomerulopathy, but post-infectious disease can look identical, so the clinical course matters.
C4d marks the classical and lectin pathways, so its absence supports a C3 glomerulopathy. But in one cohort many confirmed cases stained for C4d, so a positive C4d does not exclude it.
Mesangial IgA is not always primary. Liver cirrhosis is the most common trigger of secondary IgA nephropathy, and bowel disease and infections are others.
Back to the hook. A is a full house, the lupus pattern. B is dominant C3, despite the C4d. C needs a look for secondary causes. And the serum shows immunologic remission ahead of clinical remission.

props.title: Hook answers
lines: B Dominant C3: C4d does not exclude C3G

scenes.title: Three classic traps
scenes.altText: Three trap cards: “A single anti-PLA2R level tells the whole story” (✓ a high baseline level predicts poorer response, but monitoring needs the trend: antibody disappears before proteinuria resolves and returns before relapse); “Mesangial IgA = primary IgA nephropathy” (✓ exclude secondary causes such as cirrhosis, IBD and infection); “C4d-positive biopsy cannot be C3 glomerulopathy” (✓ C4d staining does not exclude C3 glomerulopathy; judge C3 dominance).

cues.text: Trap one: a single anti-PLA2R level tells the whole story. Not quite: a high baseline level predicts a poorer response, but monitoring needs the trend over time.
Trap two: mesangial IgA means primary IgA nephropathy. No: look for liver disease, bowel disease and infection first.
Trap three: a C4d-positive biopsy cannot be C3 glomerulopathy. No: C4d does not exclude it. Judge whether C3 dominates.

props.title: ✗ “C4d + rules out C3G.”
lines: ✓ C4d does not exclude; judge C3 dominance

scenes.title: Whole band, solo act, smoke alarm
scenes.altText: Memory aid: “Lupus brings the WHOLE BAND (full house: IgG, IgA, IgM, C3, C1q); C3 glomerulopathy is a SOLO ACT (C3 at least two steps louder than anyone else); anti-PLA2R is a SMOKE ALARM that goes quiet before the smoke clears and sounds again before the next fire.” Tokens: whole band = full house · solo act = dominant C3 · smoke alarm = PLA2R trend. A card lists where the aid breaks.

cues.text: Memory aid: lupus brings the whole band, every immunoglobulin plus C3 and C1q. C3 glomerulopathy is a solo act, with C3 two steps louder than anyone else. Anti-PLA2R is a smoke alarm: it goes quiet before the smoke clears, and sounds again before the next fire.

Where it breaks: some lupus membranous cases lack the full house; post-infectious disease can also be a C3 solo act; and the alarm can be silent early, while the kidney soaks up antibody, or in the minority of primary cases without anti-PLA2R.

scenes.title: Takeaway
scenes.altText: Two tokens: “Full house = lupus pattern · dominant C3 = C3 glomerulopathy even with C4d · mesangial IgA = exclude secondary causes”, “Anti-PLA2R: follow the trend, antibody clears before proteinuria and returns before relapse”.

cues.text: Read kidney immunofluorescence as a pattern, with a full house pointing to lupus, dominant C3 pointing to C3 glomerulopathy even when C4d stains, and mesangial IgA prompting a search for secondary causes, and follow anti-PLA2R over time rather than reading it once.

props.label: Full house = lupus · dominant C3 = C3G · IgA → secondary?
Anti-PLA2R: clears before proteinuria, returns before relapse

explanation.what: Plain language: a kidney biopsy is stained with fluorescent antibodies against immunoglobulins and complement, and each disease leaves its own pattern. In membranous nephropathy a blood test for the antibody against a podocyte protein can be followed over time. Scientific terms: direct immunofluorescence, full-house pattern (IgG, IgA, IgM, C3, C1q), membranous nephropathy, M-type phospholipase A2 receptor (PLA2R), THSD7A, immunologic remission, epitope spreading, IgA nephropathy, galactose-deficient IgA1 (Gd-IgA1), secondary IgA nephropathy, C3 glomerulopathy, dominant C3, C4d.
explanation.why: Complement pathways leave different footprints: C1q and C4d mark classical (C4d also lectin) activation, while C3 alone points to the alternative pathway. Anti-PLA2R is produced before and during active disease, binds the kidney, and is cleared before the injured podocytes recover, so the serum level leads the urine protein.
explanation.measure: Full house: IgG, IgM, IgA, C3 and C1q each at least 1+ (study definition). Dominant C3: C3c at least two steps above any other reactant on a 0, trace, 1+, 2+, 3+ scale. Anti-PLA2R: positive in about 70–80% of primary MN at presentation; measured by ELISA; serial measurement (monthly or at least every two months) during and after treatment.
explanation.differs: Full house (lupus, classical pathway) vs dominant C3 (C3 glomerulopathy, alternative pathway); immunologic remission (antibody gone) vs clinical remission (proteinuria gone); primary vs secondary IgA nephropathy (liver disease, IBD, infection).
explanation.examAngle: Expect: name the disease from an immunofluorescence description, interpret a falling or reappearing anti-PLA2R titre, or recognise that mesangial IgA or a C4d stain does not settle the diagnosis alone.

comparisons.title: Full house vs dominant C3
comparisons.distinguisher: Immunoglobulin plus C1q (classical pathway) vs C3 alone (alternative pathway).

comparisons.title: Immunologic vs clinical remission in MN
comparisons.distinguisher: Serum antibody leads; urine protein lags.

mnemonic.text: Lupus brings the WHOLE BAND (full house); C3 glomerulopathy is a SOLO ACT (C3 two steps louder than anyone else); anti-PLA2R is a SMOKE ALARM that goes quiet before the smoke clears and sounds again before the next fire.
mnemonic.explanation: Links each pattern and the antibody kinetics to one image.
mnemonic.limitation: Some lupus membranous cases lack the full house; post-infectious GN can also be C3-dominant; anti-PLA2R may be undetectable early (kidney as a sink) and is absent in a minority of primary MN.

analogyLimitations: Biopsy and timeline drawings are schematic.
The C4d figures come from one single-centre cohort; staining methods differ.
takeaway: Read kidney immunofluorescence as a pattern, with a full house pointing to lupus, dominant C3 pointing to C3 glomerulopathy even when C4d stains, and mesangial IgA prompting a search for secondary causes, and follow anti-PLA2R over time rather than reading it once.

questions.stem: A patient with PLA2R-associated membranous nephropathy reached complete remission and became anti-PLA2R negative. At a routine visit, proteinuria is still low but anti-PLA2R is detectable again. What is the best interpretation?

options.text: Possible impending relapse; continue close monitoring
options.rationale: Correct. Reappearance or a rise in anti-PLA2R signals impending relapse, sometimes before proteinuria rises.

options.text: A false-positive result, because proteinuria is low
options.rationale: Incorrect. The antibody can return before proteinuria does; low protein does not make the result false.
Incorrect. Anti-PLA2R is associated with primary MN, not evidence of a secondary cause.

options.text: No significance, because only proteinuria matters
options.rationale: Incorrect. The antibody trend is used to monitor disease activity and leads the proteinuria.

questions.stem: A biopsy shows glomerular C3 3+, IgM 1+, no IgG, IgA or C1q, and C4d 1+. There is no recent infection. Which statement is best?

options.text: This is glomerulonephritis with dominant C3; C4d staining does not exclude C3 glomerulopathy
options.rationale: Correct. C3 is two steps above IgM, meeting the consensus definition, and C4d can be present in C3 glomerulopathy.

options.text: C4d is positive, so C3 glomerulopathy is excluded
options.rationale: Incorrect. In one cohort many confirmed C3 glomerulopathy cases stained for C4d.

options.text: This is a full-house pattern typical of lupus nephritis
options.rationale: Incorrect. A full house needs IgG, IgA, IgM, C3 and C1q together.
Incorrect. IgA nephropathy needs mesangial IgA deposits, which are absent here.

questions.stem: Glomerular immunofluorescence shows IgG, IgA, IgM, C3 and C1q, each at least 1+. Which disease does this pattern classically indicate?

options.rationale: Correct. This is the full-house pattern classically seen in lupus nephritis.
Incorrect. C3 glomerulopathy shows dominant C3 with little or no immunoglobulin.
Incorrect. IgA nephropathy is mesangial IgA-dominant, and C1q is usually absent.
Incorrect. Primary MN shows granular IgG (mostly IgG4) and C3 along the basement membrane, not a full house.

references.citation: Akiyama S, Imai E, Maruyama S. Immunology of membranous nephropathy. F1000Res. 2019;8:F1000 Faculty Rev-734. doi:10.12688/f1000research.17589.1
references.usedFor: Full text read (Europe PMC). Granular IgG (IgG4) and C3 along the GBM; PLA2R and THSD7A as podocyte antigens (THSD7A 2–5%); PLA2R antibody in about 70% (70–85% across laboratories); kidney-as-a-sink phase; antibody disappears before proteinuria remission; epitope spreading from CysR to CTLD domains linked with older age and therapy resistance.

references.citation: Tesar V, Hruskova Z. Autoantibodies in the Diagnosis, Monitoring, and Treatment of Membranous Nephropathy. Front Immunol. 2021;12:593288. doi:10.3389/fimmu.2021.593288
references.usedFor: Full text read (Europe PMC). Anti-PLA2R in about 70–80% at presentation, highly specific for primary MN; measure by ELISA; immunologic remission precedes clinical remission; reappearance or rise signals impending relapse, sometimes before proteinuria; high baseline titres predict lower spontaneous remission and poorer treatment response; serial measurement monthly or at least bimonthly; epitope-specific assays not available in clinical practice.

references.citation: Pickering MC, D'Agati VD, Nester CM, et al. C3 glomerulopathy: consensus report. Kidney Int. 2013;84(6):1079-1089. doi:10.1038/ki.2013.377

references.citation: Singh G, Singh SK, Nalwa A, et al. Glomerular C4d Staining Does Not Exclude a C3 Glomerulopathy. Kidney Int Rep. 2019;4(5):698-709. doi:10.1016/j.ekir.2019.02.006
references.usedFor: Full text read (Europe PMC). C4d as a classical/lectin pathway marker whose absence supports alternative-pathway disease; C4d negative/trace in only 22% of DDD and 64% of C3GN; presence of C4d should not exclude C3 glomerulopathy.

references.citation: Ye J, Croom N, Troxell ML, et al. Non-Full House Membranous Lupus Nephritis Represents a Clinically Distinct Subset. Kidney360. 2023;4(7):935-942. doi:10.34067/kid.0000000000000161
references.usedFor: Full text read (Europe PMC). Full-house pattern (IgG, IgA, IgM, C3, C1q; kappa and lambda) as the classic lupus nephritis pattern; study definition of at least 1+ for each; existence of non-full-house membranous lupus nephritis.

references.citation: Knoppova B, Reily C, King RG, Julian BA, Novak J, Green TJ. Pathogenesis of IgA Nephropathy: Current Understanding and Implications for Development of Disease-Specific Treatment. J Clin Med. 2021;10(19):4501. doi:10.3390/jcm10194501
references.usedFor: Full text read (Europe PMC). Multi-hit pathogenesis (Gd-IgA1, IgG autoantibodies, circulating immune complexes, mesangial deposition); C3 found in most biopsies (alternative pathway) while C1 is usually absent.

references.citation: Tota M, Baron V, Musial K, et al. Secondary IgA Nephropathy and IgA-Associated Nephropathy: A Systematic Review of Case Reports. J Clin Med. 2023;12(7):2726. doi:10.3390/jcm12072726
references.usedFor: Full text read (Europe PMC). Causes of secondary IgA nephropathy (liver, gastrointestinal including IBD, infectious, autoimmune, oncological and other); liver disease, especially cirrhosis, the most common trigger.

references.citation: Wang M, Lv J, Zhang X, Chen P, Zhao M, Zhang H. Secondary IgA Nephropathy Shares the Same Immune Features With Primary IgA Nephropathy. Kidney Int Rep. 2020;5(2):165-172. doi:10.1016/j.ekir.2019.10.012
references.usedFor: Abstract and introduction read (Europe PMC full-text record). IgA nephropathy diagnosed by IgA as the dominant or co-dominant mesangial immunoglobulin, usually with C3; secondary IgA nephropathy shows Gd-IgA1 levels and deposits similar to primary disease, so the deposits alone do not separate them.

claims.text: Full house in lupus nephritis; granular IgG/C3 in MN; mesangial IgA with C3 and usually no C1q in IgAN; dominant C3 in C3G.

Anti-PLA2R in about 70–80% of primary MN, highly specific; kidney-as-sink; immunologic before clinical remission; reappearance predicts relapse; high baseline titre predicts poorer response; serial ELISA monitoring.
Epitope spreading CysR to CTLD linked with poorer response; epitope assays not routine.
Dominant C3 = at least two steps above other reactants; post-infectious GN can mimic; C4d does not exclude C3G.
Secondary IgA nephropathy causes (cirrhosis most common, IBD, infection) and shared Gd-IgA1 features.
Intense C1q as the lupus tell; no other GN shows a full house; 180 kDa PLA2R; IgAN progression rates; NIH activity/chronicity indices.
claims.note: Reviewer statements not verified in sources read this session; not taught.

claims.text: Scenario invented; biopsy and timeline drawings schematic.

accuracyFlags.issue: Ch. 55 Hit 13 calls C4d (negative/trace in 90% of C3 glomerulopathy) a clean discriminator from immune-complex GN. Singh 2019 found C4d negative/trace in only 22% of dense deposit disease and 64% of C3GN and concluded that glomerular C4d should not exclude C3 glomerulopathy (register rv-c4d-c3g-discriminator).

Ch. 55 Trap 3 presents PLA2R epitope spreading as a prognostic marker without noting that epitope-specific assays are not available in routine practice (Tesar 2021), so monitoring relies on total anti-PLA2R titres (register rv-pla2r-epitope-assay).

Ch. 55 Trap 3 frames a single anti-PLA2R level as uninformative for prognosis. Tesar 2021 notes that baseline titre does carry prognostic value: high baseline titres predict lower spontaneous remission and poorer treatment response, while serial titres are needed for monitoring remission and relapse (register rv-pla2r-baseline-titre).
